title: The Scan Is Not the Diagnosis: Can FDG PET/CT Substitute for Morphomolecular Classification in Lymphoma?
content: Purpose: In lymphoma, fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG PET/CT) establishes disease distribution and metabolic response but cannot independently determine histological identity. This Controversy examines when imaging-derived findings are sufficient for clinical action and when additional pathological evidence is required.Material and methods: A focused, non-systematic critical appraisal of lymphoma classification and clinical guidelines was integrated with selected studies of follicular lymphoma transformation and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma response.Results: Three distinct evidentiary claims require separation: tumour identity, disease distribution and the presence of actionable residual disease. Morphology, immunophenotyping and indicated genetic investigations establish biological classification; PET/CT assesses disease extent and can guide tissue selection. Among selected patients undergoing PET-directed rebiopsy, transformation was identified in seven of 29, whereas baseline maximum standardised uptake value did not predict subsequent transformation in a separate analysis of 549 patients. In a retrospective response-assessment series, viable lymphoma was demonstrated in nine of 29 biopsied PET-positive patients. These findings are context-dependent, not universal predictive values.Conclusion: A proposed three-threshold framework distinguishes tissue-based classification, imaging-directed rebiopsy and treatment-changing response assessment. Metabolic findings and morphomolecular evidence are complementary, not interchangeable; the framework itself requires prospective evaluation.
